messages:
sasha: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a sharp failure spike after we rolled promptset v7 last night.  +18% failure rate on the negation subset for rw-infer-3b-quant.
liam: ugh. Is that the prompt wording change we landed? which tests specifically?
anya: yep, looks correlated. The only diffs were a handful of clarifying sentences we added to reduce ambiguity. Example failures: model flips meaning on short negations.
sasha: pasting one failing example: 
```
PROMPT (v6): 'Does the user consent to data sharing? Answer yes or no.'
PROMPT (v7): 'Please clearly state whether the user consents to sharing their data. Answer only with yes or no.'
INPUT: 'User does not consent to sharing.'
EXPECTED: 'no'
ACTUAL: 'yes'
```
liam: hmm, that extra "Please clearly state" might be triggering the model to reframe the answer as an instruction to restate rather than classify.
eval-bot: nightly-eval results: https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/2026-03-19/pset-v7-summary (summary CSV attached). Regression metric: negation_f1 dropped from 0.92 -> 0.75, samples: 540 -> 612.
jordan: can we diff the promptset and isolate the changed prompts? I can run a canary with the v6 wording on dedicated infra if we need to validate.
sasha: I already ran a quick A/B on a 200-sample slice. v6 error rate 4% vs v7 22% on the negation subset.
anya: my hypothesis: the tokenization/quantized model sees the polite phrasing and biases toward copying the clause following punctuation. Could be an interplay with quantization temperature heuristics.
liam: plan: 1) revert the two clarifying sentences in prompt IDs: ps-1342, ps-1349 2) run nightly canary on rw-infer-3b-quant 3) open rebaseline PR if canary passes 4) if revert reduces failures but still >8%, open a deeper investigation ticket.
sasha: I opened the revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/promptsets/pull/482 (contains diff + test coverage). Can someone review? @liam @anya
liam: reviewing now. quick read: small text changes, tests cover the negation set. :thumbsup:
anya: approved, leaving a comment requesting an explicit test case for the ambiguous phrasing edge.
jordan: FYI ran the canary on dedicated with v6 wording — preliminary results: negation_f1 back to 0.91, latency unchanged. I kicked off a full-nightly rerun with the revert.
eval-bot: canary run finished: https://ci.redwood.ai/canaries/1792016800 (v6 wording on 3b-quant). metrics attached.
sasha: if full-nightly confirms, i'd like to rebaseline the promptset and mark v7 as reverted in the changelog. Also adding regression guard in CI for negation_f1 < 0.88.
liam: agreed. Assigning follow-ups: @jordan to monitor full rerun, @anya to add targeted unit test, @sasha to merge PR once green.
jordan: noted, I'll post a short postmortem in #eng-ml after the rerun completes with numbers and root cause summary.
sasha: thanks everyone. quick lesson — small wording tweaks can flip quantized models easily; let's add a short checklist before promptset changes that touch control tokens/answer-formatting. :exclamation:
